newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Bank of Portugal cuts repo rate, escudo steady.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Portugal cuts repo rate, escudo steady.

text.p: Portugal's central bank surprised markets on Friday by cutting its repurchase rate, but its move made scant impact on the escudo in currency markets.
The Bank of Portugal reduced the repurchase rate to 6.00 from 6.30 percent, the first cut in the rate since April 11 when it was lowered from 6.50 percent.
The bank offered 10 billion escudos ($58.3 million) at the repo. It also cut its drain rate to 5.70 from 5.80 percent.

Isabel Cabral, an analyst at Fincor, said the central bank probably made its move in anticipation of the April inflation figures, which are expected to be good, and an expected rate cut by the Bank of Spain next Friday.
Portugal's consumer price index (CPI) rose by 0.1 percent in March to give an annual inflation rate of 3.2 percent, unchanged from February.
Another analyst, Jorge Ferraz of Informacao Mercados Financeiros, welcomed the rate cut.

"The stance of the Bank seems intelligent to me and correct given the approach of the French elections and some exchange turbulence that could come next week in dollar-mark which would then impact the mark and the Europeans (currencies)," he said.
The escudo traded at 100.60 to the German mark after the announcement, unchanged from earlier levels. ($ = 171.6 Portugese Escudos)
